slides.title: Basic Plotting
slides.content:
# Hello Plot 📈

`pyplot` is the main interface.

```matplotlib
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

x = [1, 2, 3]
y = [2, 4, 6]

plt.plot(x, y) # Line plot
plt.show()
```

## Common Types
- `plt.bar(x, y)`: Bar Chart
- `plt.scatter(x, y)`: Scatter Plot
- `plt.hist(data)`: Histogram

slides.title: Customization
slides.content:
# Make it Pretty 🎨

Always label your axes!

```matplotlib
plt.plot(x, y, color='red', linestyle='--', marker='o')
plt.title("Sales Growth")
plt.xlabel("Year")
plt.ylabel("Revenue ($)")
plt.grid(True)
```

slides.title: Subplots
slides.content:
# Multiple Plots 🖼️

Using the Object-Oriented interface (recommended for complex plots).

```matplotlib
fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2) # 1 row, 2 cols

ax1.plot(x, y)
ax1.set_title("Plot 1")

ax2.bar(x, y)
ax2.set_title("Plot 2")

plt.show()
```
